root_cause.text: The `__rlookup_amd_iommu()` function indexes into `rlookup_table[devid]` without first verifying that `devid` is within the valid range defined by `pci_seg->last_bdf`, allowing an out-of-bounds read when a PCI device's BDF is not described by the IVRS.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds the bounds check `if (devid > pci_seg->last_bdf) return NULL;` before the array access, and the commit message states that "the lookup reads past the end of the allocation before the caller's bounds check can run." The CVE description details that this out-of-bounds read, after a memory allocation change to `kvcalloc()`, causes a general protection fault by returning adjacent slab contents that are then dereferenced as a `struct amd_iommu *`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a bounds check to guard against out-of-range device ID when looking up AMD IOMMU per segment, returning NULL if the device is not described by IVRS.
intent_record.what: Changed the loop condition to use inequality and continue, and added a check to return NULL if devid exceeds pci_seg->last_bdf before indexing into rlookup_table.
intent_record.how: Prevents out-of-bounds access on the rlookup_table array by ensuring devid is within the valid range described by the IVRS; returns NULL instead of a potentially invalid pointer.

relevance_review.reason: The change adds a bounds check to verify devid against pci_seg->last_bdf before indexing rlookup_table, directly preventing the out-of-bounds read described in the vulnerability root cause.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement indexes into rlookup_table using devid without proper bounds checking beyond a simple greater-than check, allowing an out-of-bounds read when devid is not within the valid range defined by the allocated array size, as per the vulnerability root cause.
